title: Uniform gradients of quadratic feature-law potentials
source_anchor: Samplinglib original sphere geometry and feature-law supplement v1, 2026-10-23; exact units[1] and complete formula proof
target_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure and H a complete real inner-product normed space. Let F:E→H have actual ambient Frechet derivative D(w):E→H for every w. Assume nonnegative M1,M2, an operator bound norm(D(w))<=M1 on the closed unit ball and an operator-Lipschitz bound norm(D(w)-D(u))<=M2 norm(w-u) there. Fix y in H. On the actual unit-norm subtype S define K(w)=F(w), angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)), the actual Bochner mean m(mu)=integral K dmu, V_mu(w)=2 inner(m(mu)-y,F(w)), and G_mu(w)=2P_w D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) with the explicit projection P_w z=z−⟨z,w⟩w, which projects onto w-perpendicular when norm(w)=1. Let Q(mu,nu) be the literal extended nonnegative infimum of the quadratic angular cost over all actual couplings. There exist C1,C2>0, independent of probability laws and unit weights, such that for every actual parameter probability K is integrable, V_mu has the displayed ambient gradient 2D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) at every ambient w, and its projected G_mu is tangent and uniformly bounded by C1 at every unit weight. For every two actual parameter probabilities Q is finite and norm(G_mu(w)-G_nu(u))<=C2*(sqrt(Q).toReal+c(w,u)). Feature boundedness, strong measurability, feature Lipschitz control and residual budgets are derived inside the proof rather than assumed; the returned conclusions are feature integrability, actual ambient gradient, tangency/uniform bound, finite transport cost and the joint sensitivity estimate. The constants may depend on the displayed feature/derivative data, E,H and y. This is a generic feature-law theorem, not a concrete Gaussian scalar-data potential, installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API or intrinsic path-length theorem.
